title: Runtime Operational Tuning and Triage Playbook
author: Maya Chen
summary: A practical playbook that brings together runtime architecture patterns, kernel-scheduler knobs, profiling procedures, and benchmark guidance to support tuning and regression triage for the inference runtime (v2.8+). Intended for SREs, runtime engineers, and applied ML owners.
scope: Applies to hosted and dedicated clusters using the main runtime image. Excludes driver-level debugging (NVDriver/ROCm internals) and customer-specific VPC networking changes.
goals_and_target_slos:
- Small models (<512 tokens) p99 <= 50 ms
- Medium models (512-2048) p99 <= 200 ms
- Long sequences (>2048) p99 <= 600 ms
- Cost target: <= 1.5x per-token cost vs baseline quantized profile
- Regression sensitivity: detect +10% p99 or +20% per-token cost change within 3 hours
key_components: rt-agent (diagnostics & snapshotting), kernel-scheduler (priority-driven executor v3), perfbench (bench & replay), kvcache-coop (KV cache service), observability (Prometheus, OTLP->Jaeger, Loki)
benchmark_matrix:
Workload | Model | Seq len dist | Concurrency | Expected p50 | Expected p99 | Notes
small-chat | llama-7b-q4 | 16/64/128 | 100 qps | ~18ms | ~48ms | baseline small mix
summarization | llama-13b-fp16 | 256/512 | 40 qps | ~120ms | ~370ms | benefits from KV reuse
retrieval-aug | mix-ensemble | 32/256 | 60 qps | ~45ms | ~220ms | mixed routing
kernel_scheduling_knobs: kernel-concurrency-limit (default 32): caps concurrent kernel launches per GPU; priority-weights (interactive, background, batch): protect interactive traffic; continuous-batch-window-ms (3-20 ms): tradeoff throughput vs tail latency; prefetch-kv-policy: eager|lazy|adaptive; quant-select-policy: auto|force-8bit|force-fp16
profiling_playbook_steps:
1) Alert fires for p99 or per-token-cost delta.
2) Trigger rt-agent snapshot for affected shard(s)  (metrics, traces, profiler).
3) Reproduce with perfbench using matching seq-dist and concurrency.
4) Correlate spans in Jaeger: look for kernel-queueing, kernel-launch, device-sync, memcpy.
5) If device stalls suspected, collect Nsight/ROCm capture on worst shard.
6) Apply fast mitigations (adjust scheduler weights, increase kernel-concurrency-limit, enable fallback kernel) and evaluate.
7) Assign RCA owners and collect artifacts (replay config, traces, nsight captures).
regression_triage_flow:
1) Isolate: single shard vs fleet-wide via topology-mapper.
2) Check recent changes: runtime release, kernel variants, quantization, infra drivers.
3) Reproduce: perfbench replay with --match-headers --seed. If unreproducible, run 30m production replay in staging.
4) Categorize: scheduler, kernel, memory, or KV/network.
5) Short-term rollback: revert runtime image for affected pools if change in last 72h.
testing_checklist_before_rollout:
- Kernel unit tests (kernel-suite v2) green
- Perfbench sweep (3 seeds) statistical check: p50/p90/p99 within safety bounds (-5%/+8%)
- End-to-end replay 10 minutes with tracing
- Cost-account run to validate per-token cost delta
- Canary stages: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with hold windows 30/60/120 minutes
rollout_guardrails:
Use feature flags: feature.kernel_variant and feature.scheduler_profile.
Canary metrics: p99 latency, CPU steal, device SM util, kernel-queue-length, kvcache-hit-rate. All must be within thresholds to proceed.
ownership_and_escalation:
First-line: runtime-oncall (SRE) - initial detection and quick mitigation.
Second-line: runtime-platform (kernel-scheduler & mapper).
Third-line: applied-ml (model regressions) or vendor-support (driver).
Escalation timeline: initial triage within 30 minutes, RCA assignment within 8 hours, RCA writeup within 72 hours.
appendix_B_acceptance_criteria:
- No p99 regression > 10% in canary window.
- No per-token cost increase > 15% at steady-state.
- No new class of OOM/eviction observed in the canary fleet.
